title: Effect of additional patient information on preoperative anxiety in children with support from a dog-assisted intervention - a randomized controlled trial
summary:
In medical literature, it is reported that 40–70% of children undergoing surgery under general anesthesia experience anxiety beforehand. Anxiety in the preoperative period is associated with a higher risk of emergence delirium, behavioral disturbances, increased pain, and greater medication requirements both during and after surgery. Reducing anxiety before surgery is therefore important to improve care for pediatric patients.
Previous studies suggest that animal-assisted interventions, particularly those involving dogs, can help reduce stress and anxiety in patients. However, there are currently no data on the effect of such interventions on preoperative anxiety in children.
The aim of this project is to evaluate the potential effects of a preoperative anesthesia orientation session with a therapy dog on children’s anxiety before surgery.
As part of this session, children are introduced to anesthesia in a child-friendly and age-appropriate way, supported by a trained therapy dog.
All children receive standard preoperative care. Participants are randomly assigned to either a control group or an intervention group. Children in the intervention group are additionally invited to attend the next available preoperative anaesthesia orientation session before their surgery. On the day of surgery, anxiety is assessed at the entrance to the operating area using validated psychological scales. Data collection ends with a survey of guardians after the child has been handed over to the care team.
conditions: preoperative anxiety at the operating theatre entrance

interventions.name:
Intervention group:
After inclusion in the study, participation in the intervention "preoperative anesthesia orientation session for children with a therapy dog" before the day of surgery

Control group:
no further intervention after inclusion in the study

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Child attends school (at least primary school)
Planned, elective surgery in the central operating theatre of the University Hospital RWTH Aachen
General anaesthesia with ventilation
Guardian's informed consent 
According to the guardian, the child is able to participate in a child-friendly and age-appropriate preoperative anesthesia orientation session as planned in the study 
A preoperative anesthesia orientation session takes place before the planned surgery date  
Availability of the child and guardians to attend the scheduled intervention session
Exclusion criteria:
Child or guardian refuses participation 
Guardian unable to give consent 
Child or guardian with language barrier 
Child under legal guardianship 
Guardian under legal guardianship 
Child with ASA grade III – V  
Child has already undergone surgery
Emergency surgery
Child takes anxiolytics
Child with allergy to dogs
Child is afraid of dogs
